the computer‐aided case‐history‐taking system is reliable, accurate, and efficient in the identification and recording of primary and secondary patient complaints.

a computer‐based system can conduct the case‐history interview in eye examinations and can identify the primary and secondary complaints with reliability comparable to that of experienced human interviewers.
the system is capable of identifying 90% of all primary complaints and 80% of all secondary complaints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a system for the automatic collection and analysis of medical data from a patient.
the development of an automatic system for the case‐history interview in the eye clinic.
the design and evaluation of an automatic case history taker.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is a useful adjunct to the clinical interview, particularly in the hands of inexperienced personnel, and that it has a potential use as a screening instrument.
an automatic case history taker is feasible, and that it can be used successfully for the purpose of identifying the patient's complaints.
the system is a reliable and useful aid in conducting the case history portion of the eye examination, and has the potential of becoming an important tool for ophthalmic diagnosis and treatment.

a system such as this, which can be easily and economically installed and maintained in a medical setting, is useful for the purpose of case‐history interviewing.
